what: Follow-up to 01435 (lead 20:27): take the thread-local cost back off the query-hit path. 01435 made every thread-local read #[inline(never)], including db::local::with (was #[inline(always)]), so each with is now one call, because a fiber job may resume on another thread and an inlined read could keep the old thread address across a wait. Instead, read the job state pointer once at job start and after each suspend, not per with: e.g. each job (and each non-fiber thread) owns its Local/Stacks behind a pointer, held in one place that the fiber switch rewrites (the carried put, or a field of the fiber Cx that code reaches without re-reading TLS), so the hit path does one plain load of a pointer it already holds, and only the switch code touches TLS. Keep correct first: no address of a thread-local may survive a wait (a test that waits between two withs in one function on a 1-core driver, with another job writing its own stack meanwhile, must find its own frames), and no fallback. Measure the hit path before and after with the query_hit bench (blaze-bench, held by query-unify: ask them).
